faq: What should an invoice include in Nigeria?

Your business name and contact, the customer’s name, an invoice number, the date, what they are buying with quantities and prices, the total, and how to pay you. If you charge VAT, show it on its own line.
How do I save the invoice as a PDF?
Tap “Print or save as PDF”. On a phone or computer, pick “Save as PDF” as the printer. Only the invoice prints, not the rest of the page.
What is the difference between an invoice and a receipt?
An invoice asks for payment. A receipt shows the customer has paid. Use the free receipt generator once the money is in.
Can Shopinbos make invoices for me?

title: VAT calculator (Nigeria 7.5%)
excerpt: Add 7.5% VAT to a price, or take VAT out of a price that already includes it. Shows the amount before VAT, the VAT and the total.
meta_title: VAT calculator Nigeria (7.5%): add or remove VAT | Shopinbos
meta_description: Free Nigerian VAT calculator: add 7.5% VAT to a price or work out the VAT inside a price. In naira and kobo, with the sum shown.
steps: Type the amount.
Choose “Add VAT” if your price does not include VAT yet, or “Take VAT out” if it already does.
Read the amount before VAT, the VAT and the amount with VAT.
more: Nigeria’s VAT rate is 7.5%. To add VAT, multiply by 0.075. To find the VAT inside a price, divide the price by 1.075 and take that away from the price.
faq: How do I calculate 7.5% VAT?
Multiply the price by 0.075. On ₦20,000, the VAT is ₦1,500 and the price with VAT is ₦21,500.
How do I remove VAT from a price?
Divide the price by 1.075. ₦21,500 ÷ 1.075 is ₦20,000, so the VAT inside it is ₦1,500.
Do I have to charge VAT?
It depends on your business and what you sell. Check with the tax office or an accountant. VAT is added where it applies.
Can Shopinbos add VAT at checkout?
Yes. In Shopinbos Business you choose how VAT is added at checkout and whether it shows on receipts and invoices.

Is the charge added on top or taken out?
Both happen. Some agents debit the amount plus the charge, others give you the amount minus the charge. Pick the one your agent uses.
How much does a POS agent keep?
The charge minus what the POS provider or bank takes. Check your provider’s app for their cut, add it here, and the calculator shows what you keep.

Start from what delivery costs you for each area, add a small amount for packing, and round to a clean figure. Heavier parcels cost more, so add a charge per extra kg.
Should I offer free delivery?
Only above an order amount where your profit can cover it. Free delivery above a set amount often makes customers add one more item.

steps: Type what one item costs you.
Pick “The markup I want” and type a percentage, or pick “My selling price” and type your price.
Read the selling price, your profit per item, and the markup and margin.
more: Markup is profit as a share of the cost. Margin is profit as a share of the selling price. A 100% markup is a 50% margin, so always check which one people mean.
faq: What is the difference between markup and margin?
Markup is profit ÷ cost. Margin is profit ÷ price. If an item costs ₦5,000 and sells for ₦8,000, the markup is 60% and the margin is 37.5%.
What markup should I use?
Many small shops use 40% to 100% on the product cost, then check the margin still covers delivery, packaging and payment fees.
How do I turn a margin into a markup?
Markup = margin ÷ (100 − margin) × 100. A 40% margin is about a 67% markup.

steps: Pick ajo or esusu (members take turns) or daily thrift with a collector.

Add members’ names in order if you like, then copy or share the schedule.
more: In ajo or esusu, everyone pays the same amount each round and one member collects the whole pot. In daily thrift, you save daily with a collector who keeps an agreed share, often one day’s savings, as the fee.
faq: How does ajo work?
Each member pays the same amount every week or month. Each round, one member collects everything paid in that round, until everyone has collected once.
How much is each payout?
Members × the amount each pays, minus any organiser fee. Ten members paying ₦10,000 gives a ₦100,000 payout.
How does daily thrift (alajo) work?
You pay a collector a fixed amount every day for a cycle, often a month. At the end you get your savings back, minus the share the collector keeps.
Is ajo safe?
Only with people you trust. Write down who collects when, share the schedule with every member, and keep records of every payment.

Short (under eight words), easy to remember and true to what you sell. Read it out loud: if it sounds natural, it works.
Do I need a slogan?
No, but it helps people remember you and what you stand for, especially on flyers and packaging.
Can I change my slogan later?
Yes. Update it on your store, social pages and packaging when you are ready.
